evals.name: bant-eval-1
evals.expected_output: Budget is Missed or Partial (no number, Ellen explicitly says she doesn't have one from Tom). Authority is Partial (Ellen has a green light from managing partner Tom but is not the final decision-maker herself). Need is Covered (the specific two-day-lost-document incident, and the scaling-from-six-to-fourteen detail). Timeline is Covered (the six-week tax-season deadline). Closes with a single Advance / Advance-with-follow-up / Do-not-advance call, most plausibly 'advance with a follow-up on budget', not a full recap of all four.
expectations: All four BANT criteria receive a Status
Budget is scored Missed or Partial, not Covered, since Ellen states she has no number
Need is scored Covered and cites the specific lost-document incident or the six-to-fourteen scaling detail
Timeline is scored Covered and cites the six-week deadline
Closes with a single advance/no-advance call and the one thing that would change it, not a restated summary
Cites at least one specific, concrete detail from the transcript (a number, name, or quoted phrase) rather than a generic paraphrase that could apply to any call

evals.name: bant-eval-2-reads-well-too
evals.prompt: run bant on a transcript of a first call that clearly surfaced strong signal on all four BANT criteria
evals.expected_output: The audit scores all four as Covered rather than nitpicking a genuinely strong call into Partials. The reads-well-too check is applied before finalizing.
expectations: A genuinely strong call is not scored as mostly Partial or Missed
The reads-well-too check from references/rubric.md is applied before the audit is finalized

evals.name: bant-eval-3-csv
evals.prompt: run bant on a CRM pipeline export csv with deal rows missing several BANT fields
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a structural hygiene sweep, not a call-quality audit, and says so explicitly. Flags each deal row for missing BANT-relevant fields. Output is a table sorted by deal value descending. Makes no claim about what was actually discussed on any specific call.
expectations: States explicitly that CSV mode is a structural check, not a call-quality claim
Output is sorted by deal value descending
Does not claim to know what happened on any specific call from CRM fields alone
